Django

Complete Reference & Concept Guide v5.2.x Python 3.12+ Released Dec 2025

Django is a high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design. This guide covers models, views, templates, REST APIs, and everything in between.

Installation & Setup

# Create virtual environment & install Django
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install Django
pip install django

# Pin version for reproducibility
pip install django==5.2.0

# Create a new project
django-admin startproject myproject
cd myproject

# Create an app
python manage.py startapp blog

# Run development server
python manage.py runserver

# Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/

Project Structure

Django follows a "project" (site) + "app" (module) pattern.

Typical Project Layout
myproject/                  # Project root (git repo)
├─ manage.py             # CLI entry point
├─ myproject/            # Project config package
│   ├─ __init__.py
│   ├─ settings.py        # Configuration
│   ├─ urls.py            # Root URL configuration
│   ├─ asgi.py            # ASGI entry for async
│   ├─ wsgi.py            # WSGI entry for production
│   ├─ celery.py          # Celery config (optional)
├─ apps/                # All Django apps
│   ├─ blog/
│   │   ├─ __init__.py
│   │   ├─ admin.py        # Admin config
│   │   ├─ apps.py         # App config class
│   │   ├─ models.py       # Database models
│   │   ├─ views.py        # Request handlers
│   │   ├─ urls.py         # App-specific URLs
│   │   ├─ serializers.py  # DRF serializers
│   │   ├─ services.py     # Business logic
│   │   ├─ tests.py
│   │   ├─ filters.py      # django-filter
│   │   ├─ pagination.py   # Custom pagination
│   │   ├─ permissions.py  # DRF permissions
│   │   ├─ templates/
│   │   │   ├─ blog/
│   │   │       ├─ post_list.html
│   │   │       ├─ post_detail.html
│   │   ├─ migrations/
│   │       ├─ __init__.py
│   │       ├─ 0001_initial.py
│   ├─ users/
│       ...
├─ static/              # Global static files
├─ media/               # User-uploaded files
├─ templates/           # Global templates
├─ requirements/
│   ├─ base.txt

├─ .env                  # Environment variables
├─ .gitignore

Models & ORM

Django's ORM maps Python classes to database tables. Each model is a subclass of django.db.models.Model.

Defining Models
from django.db import models
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model

User = get_user_model()

class Category(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100, unique=True)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=120, unique=True)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)

    class Meta:
        verbose_name_plural = "categories"
        ordering = ["name"]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

class Post(models.Model):
    # Field types
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    slug = models.SlugField(max_length=250, unique=True)
    content = models.TextField()
    excerpt = models.TextField(blank=True)

    # Relationships
    author = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="posts")
    category = models.ForeignKey(Category, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True)
    tags = models.ManyToManyField("Tag", blank=True)

    # Timestamps
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    published_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)

    # Status choices
    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        DRAFT = "draft", "Draft"
        PUBLISHED = "published", "Published"
        ARCHIVED = "archived", "Archived"

    status = models.CharField(
        max_length=10, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.DRAFT
    )

    class Meta:
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["slug"]),
            models.Index(fields=["-created_at"]),
        ]
        ordering = ["-created_at"]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
ORM Query Reference
# CRUD
post = Post.objects.create(title="Hello", author=user)
post = Post(title="Hello", author=user); post.save()
post.title = "Updated"; post.save()
post.delete()

# Retrieval
Post.objects.all()                            # all records
Post.objects.get(slug="hello-world")           # single record
Post.objects.filter(status="published")         # filtered queryset
Post.objects.exclude(status="archived")        # exclude

# Chaining & lazy evaluation
qs = Post.objects.filter(author=user)
qs = qs.exclude(status="draft")
qs = qs.select_related("author")              # join (FK)
qs = qs.prefetch_related("tags")             # join (M2M)

# Field lookups
qs = Post.objects.filter(title__icontains="django")
qs = Post.objects.filter(created_at__year=2026)
qs = Post.objects.filter(author__email__endswith="@example.com")

# Aggregation & annotation
from django.db.models import Count, Sum, Avg, F, Q

Post.objects.filter(author=user).count()
Category.objects.annotate(post_count=Count("post"))
Post.objects.filter(Q(status="published") | Q(status="draft"))

# Advanced
qs = Post.objects.select_for_update()          # row lock
qs = Post.objects.defer("content")           # lazy load field
qs = Post.objects.only("title", "slug")      # only these fields
Migrations
# After changing models:
python manage.py makemigrations
python manage.py migrate

# Revert last migration
python manage.py migrate app_name 0001_previous

# Show SQL for a migration
python manage.py sqlmigrate blog 0003

# Fake a migration (already applied in DB)
python manage.py migrate --fake

Views (FBV & CBV)

Views handle HTTP requests and return responses. Django supports function-based views (FBV) and class-based views (CBV).

Function-Based Views
from django.shortcuts import render, get_object_or_404, redirect
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods
from .models import Post

# Simple view
def post_list(request):
    posts = Post.objects.filter(status="published")
    context = {"posts": posts}
    return render(request, "blog/post_list.html", context)

# View with URL parameter
def post_detail(request, slug):
    post = get_object_or_404(Post, slug=slug, status="published")
    return render(request, "blog/post_detail.html", {"post": post})

# Decorators for auth & HTTP methods
@login_required
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def post_create(request):
    if request.method == "POST":
        # handle form
        ...
    return render(request, "blog/post_form.html")
Class-Based Views (CBV)
from django.views import generic
from django.urls import reverse_lazy
from .models import Post
from .forms import PostForm

class PostListView(generic.ListView):
    model = Post
    queryset = Post.objects.filter(status="published")
    template_name = "blog/post_list.html"
    context_object_name = "posts"
    paginate_by = 10

class PostDetailView(generic.DetailView):
    model = Post
    template_name = "blog/post_detail.html"
    slug_field = "slug"
    slug_url_kwarg = "slug"

class PostCreateView(generic.CreateView):
    model = Post
    form_class = PostForm
    template_name = "blog/post_form.html"
    success_url = reverse_lazy("blog:post_list")

    def form_valid(self, form):
        form.instance.author = self.request.user
        return super().form_valid(form)

class PostUpdateView(generic.UpdateView):
    model = Post
    form_class = PostForm
    template_name = "blog/post_form.html"

class PostDeleteView(generic.DeleteView):
    model = Post
    success_url = reverse_lazy("blog:post_list")

URL Routing

# myproject/urls.py (root)
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include
from django.conf import settings
from django.conf.urls.static import static

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),
    path("api/", include("apps.blog.urls")),
    path("api/auth/", include("apps.users.urls")),
]

# Serve media in development
if settings.DEBUG:
    urlpatterns += static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT)


# apps/blog/urls.py (app)
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = "blog"

urlpatterns = [
    # FBW
    path("", views.post_list, name="post_list"),
    path("<slug:slug>/", views.post_detail, name="post_detail"),

    # CBV
    path("", views.PostListView.as_view(), name="post_list"),
    path("create/", views.PostCreateView.as_view(), name="post_create"),
    path("<slug:slug>/update/", views.PostUpdateView.as_view(), name="post_update"),
    path("<slug:slug>/delete/", views.PostDeleteView.as_view(), name="post_delete"),
]

Templates

Django's template language is HTML with special tags and filters. Use DTL by default or Jinja2 as an alternative.

Template Tags & Filters
{# base.html â€” template inheritance #}
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>{% block title %}My Site{% endblock %}</title>
</head>
<body>
    {% block content %}{% endblock %}
</body>
</html>

{# post_list.html #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block content %}
    <h1>Blog Posts</h1>
    {% for post in posts %}
        <article>
            <h2><a href="{% url 'blog:post_detail' slug=post.slug %}">
                {{ post.title }}
            </a></h2>
            <p>{{ post.excerpt|truncatewords:30 }}</p>
            <small>{{ post.created_at|date:"F j, Y" }}</small>
        </article>
    {% empty %}
        <p>No posts yet.</p>
    {% endfor %}

    {% if is_paginated %}
        <nav>
            {% if page_obj.has_previous %}
                <a href="?page={{ page_obj.previous_page_number }}">Prev</a>
            {% endif %}
            <span>Page {{ page_obj.number }} of {{ page_obj.paginator.num_pages }}</span>
            {% if page_obj.has_next %}
                <a href="?page={{ page_obj.next_page_number }}">Next</a>
            {% endif %}
        </nav>
    {% endif %}
{% endblock %}

Forms

from django import forms
from .models import Post

# Form from model (ModelForm)
class PostForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Post
        fields = ["title", "content", "category", "tags", "status"]
        widgets = {
            "content": forms.Textarea(attrs={"class": "ckeditor", "rows": 10}),
        }
        labels = {
            "title": "Post Title",
        }

    def clean_title(self):
        # Field-level validation
        title = self.cleaned_data["title"]
        if len(title) < 5:
            raise forms.ValidationError("Title too short")
        return title

# Manual form (Form)
class ContactForm(forms.Form):
    name = forms.CharField(max_length=100)
    email = forms.EmailField()
    message = forms.CharField(widget=forms.Textarea)

    def clean_email(self):
        email = self.cleaned_data["email"]
        if "@example.com" not in email:
            raise forms.ValidationError("Only example.com allowed")
        return email

# In view
def contact(request):
    form = ContactForm(request.POST or None)
    if request.method == "POST" and form.is_valid():
        print(form.cleaned_data)  # {'name': ..., 'email': ..., 'message': ...}
        return redirect("thanks")
    return render(request, "contact.html", {"form": form})

Authentication

# settings.py
AUTH_USER_MODEL = "users.User"   # custom user model
LOGIN_URL = "login"
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = "home"

# apps/users/models.py â€” Custom User Model
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models

class User(AbstractUser):
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)
    avatar = models.ImageField(upload_to="avatars/", blank=True)
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=15, blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.email

# Built-in auth views (django.contrib.auth.urls)
urlpatterns = [
    path("accounts/", include("django.contrib.auth.urls")),
]
# Provides: login, logout, password_change, password_reset, etc.

# Login decorators & mixins
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.contrib.auth.mixins import LoginRequiredMixin

@login_required
def dashboard(request):
    ...

class DashboardView(LoginRequiredMixin, generic.TemplateView):
    template_name = "dashboard.html"
▶ Best Practice: Always set AUTH_USER_MODEL before the first migration. Custom user models make it easy to add fields later.

Django REST Framework

DRF is the most popular library for building RESTful APIs with Django.

# serializers.py
from rest_framework import serializers
from .models import Post, Category

class CategorySerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Category
        fields = ["id", "name", "slug"]

class PostListSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    author_name = serializers.ReadOnlyField(source="author.get_full_name")

    class Meta:
        model = Post
        fields = [
            "id", "title", "slug", "excerpt",
            "author_name", "status", "created_at",
        ]

class PostDetailSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    category = CategorySerializer(read_only=True)
    tags = serializers.StringRelatedField(many=True)
    author = serializers.HiddenField(default=serializers.CurrentUserDefault())

    class Meta:
        model = Post
        fields = "__all__"

# views.py (API views)
from rest_framework import viewsets, permissions, filters, generics
from django_filters.rest_framework import DjangoFilterBackend

class PostViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.select_related("author", "category")
    serializer_class = PostDetailSerializer
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly]
    filter_backends = [DjangoFilterBackend, filters.SearchFilter, filters.OrderingFilter]
    filterset_fields = ["status", "category__slug"]
    search_fields = ["title", "content"]
    ordering_fields = ["created_at", "title"]

    def get_serializer_class(self):
        if self.action == "list":
            return PostListSerializer
        return PostDetailSerializer

    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        serializer.save(author=self.request.user)

# urls.py
from rest_framework.routers import DefaultRouter
router = DefaultRouter()
router.register("posts", views.PostViewSet)
urlpatterns = router.urls

Middleware & Signals

Custom Middleware
# middleware.py
import time
from django.utils.deprecation import MiddlewareMixin

class RequestTimingMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        response = self.get_response(request)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        print(f"Request took {elapsed:.3f}s")
        return response

# settings.py
MIDDLEWARE.insert(0, "myproject.middleware.RequestTimingMiddleware")
Signals
# signals.py
from django.db.models.signals import post_save, pre_delete
from django.dispatch import receiver
from .models import Post

@receiver(post_save, sender=Post)
def post_saved(sender, instance, created, **kwargs):
    if created:
        print(f"New post created: {instance.title}")
    else:
        print(f"Post updated: {instance.title}")

Testing

Django's test runner extends unittest with web-specific helpers.

from django.test import TestCase, Client
from django.urls import reverse
from .models import Post

class PostModelTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create_user("testuser", "test@example.com")

    def test_create_post(self):
        post = Post.objects.create(
            title="Test Post",
            slug="test-post",
            content="Content here",
            author=self.user,
        )
        self.assertEqual(post.__str__(), "Test Post")
        self.assertEqual(post.status, "draft")

class PostViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.client = Client()
        self.user = User.objects.create_user("testuser", "test@example.com")

    def test_post_list_status(self):
        url = reverse("blog:post_list")
        response = self.client.get(url)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertTemplateUsed(response, "blog/post_list.html")

    def test_create_post_requires_login(self):
        url = reverse("blog:post_create")
        response = self.client.get(url)
        self.assertRedirects(response, "/accounts/login/?next=" + url)

# DRF API tests
from rest_framework.test import APITestCase, APIClient

class PostAPITest(APITestCase):
    def test_list_posts(self):
        response = self.client.get("/api/posts/")
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
▶ Run tests: python manage.py test — python manage.py test --parallel — python manage.py test apps.blog.tests.test_views

Best Practices

Project Structure
  • Use a custom AUTH_USER_MODEL from the start
  • Separate apps by domain: users, blog, payments
  • Keep views thin â€” move logic to services.py
  • Use select_related / prefetch_related to avoid N+1
  • Store secrets in environment variables, not settings
  • Use python-decouple or django-environ
Security
  • Always use {% csrf_token %} in forms
  • Set SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT in production
  • Use ContentSecurityPolicy middleware
  • Never trust user input â€” always validate
  • Use @require_POST or @login_required appropriately
  • Set SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True
Performance
  • Add database indexes thoughtfully
  • Use select_related for FK/O2O relationships
  • Use prefetch_related for M2M/reverse FK
  • Cache expensive queries with cache.set()
  • Use django-debug-toolbar during development
  • Serve static/media via CDN in production
Deployment
  • Use Gunicorn + Nginx for production
  • Use Whitenoise for static files
  • Set DEBUG = False and configure ALLOWED_HOSTS
  • Use PostgreSQL (not SQLite) in production
  • Run collectstatic during deployment
  • Use Celery for background tasks
